1	# Session 203 — D48 BC endomotive Galois orbits on χ_P-projected KMS_∞ ground states
2	
3	**Date:** 2026-04-28
4	**Mode:** wild_swing / frontier attack on ATTACK_VECTORS §D.D48
5	**Target:** D48 — Connes-Consani-Marcolli endomotive Galois orbits of
6	χ_P-projected KMS_∞ ground states of the Bost-Connes system
7	**Critic-recommended pick:** S163 (post-S162) and S192 (post-S164–S191)
8	both flagged D48 as the highest-A-prior open vector for non-commutative
9	arithmetic invariants. S201 critique (post-S200, A-grade drought 0/40)
10	again pushed for D48 or A7 plethysm. This session takes the D48 swing.
11	**Channelled mathematician:** Connes (noncommutative geometry,
12	endomotive formalism — CCM 2007 §6.2 trace-vs-ground-state distinction).
13	**Self-grade:** **B** (case (i) — first project measurement of a
14	non-commutative-arithmetic invariant on χ_P at the BC ground-state
15	level, structurally distinct from the trace-level CLOSED line 185;
16	adds a new orthogonal pseudorandomness category — the 14th — but lands
17	at the matched-density noise floor across the entire tested range).
18	
19	## What was produced
20	
21	1. `experiments/algebraic/bc_endomotive_galois_chi_p/bc_endomotive_galois_chi_p.py`
22	   — full implementation: cyclic decomposition of `(Z/NZ)*` via
23	   CRT-lifted prime-power generators, character-tuple enumeration
24	   on `Π_i Z/d_i`, exact `S_χ(ω) := Σ_p ω(p)` evaluation in `Z[ζ_M]`
25	   (`M = exp G`) with both numerical-threshold and exact-cyclotomic
26	   zero detection, Galois-orbit decomposition under
27	   `(Z/MZ)*`-action, equivalence-class structure under the χ_P-corner
28	   projection, 50-trial random matched-density null, z-score on
29	   `n_zero` and per-bin orbit-length histogram.
30	2. `bc_endomotive_galois_chi_p_results.md` — pre-stated falsification
31	   criterion (cases I, E, B-grade-success, A-grade-success, INC),
32	   results table across 14 moduli, finite-size diagnosis of N=60
33	   anomaly, closure summary.
34	3. `bc_endomotive_galois_chi_p_results.json` — raw measurement data.
35	4. **EDGES.md E2.30** added (line 2837 onward) — 14th orthogonal
36	   pseudorandomness category for χ_P at the BC ground-state level.
37	5. **CLOSED_PATHS.md row** added (after line 826).
38	6. **ATTACK_VECTORS.md** D48 marked `[CLOSED S203, see "Closed
39	   attacks"]` with PARTIAL CLOSURE summary inline; full entry
40	   appended to the `## Closed attacks` section at the top of that
41	   block.
42	7. **CROSS_DOMAIN_TECHNIQUES.md** row "Connes-Consani-Marcolli
43	   endomotive" upgraded `PROPOSED (D48)` → `USED-E (S203 edge
44	   E2.30)`.
45	8. **Two successor entries proposed** (per autonomy invariant
46	   self-extension rule): D49 (BC at finite β, type III Hecke factor)
47	   and D50 (CMR 2005 imaginary-quadratic class fields, complex
48	   multiplication). Both pivot to different cross-domain ingredients
49	   that would not duplicate the present (E) closure.
50	
51	## The mathematical content (one paragraph)
52	
53	Truncate the BC C*-algebra to the commutative subalgebra
54	`\mathcal{A}_N := \mathbb{C}[(\mathbb{Z}/N\mathbb{Z})^*]`. The pure
55	KMS_∞ ground states are `\phi_\omega(\delta_a) = \omega(a)` for
56	characters `\omega \in \widehat{G}`, `G = (\mathbb{Z}/N\mathbb{Z})^*`,
57	with the cyclotomic Galois group `(\mathbb{Z}/M\mathbb{Z})^*`
58	(`M = \exp G`) acting via `\sigma_a \cdot \omega = \omega^a`
59	(Hilbert-12 truncation). The χ_P-projector
60	`P_\chi := \sum_{p \leq N \text{ prime}, \gcd(p,N) = 1} \delta_p \in
61	\mathcal{A}_N` defines a corner subalgebra `P_\chi \mathcal{A}_N P_\chi`;
62	the projected functional `\omega(P_\chi a P_\chi) = \omega(P_\chi)^2 \cdot
63	\omega(a)` distinguishes characters according to whether
64	`S_\chi(\omega) := \omega(P_\chi) = \sum_p \omega(p)` vanishes. The
65	zero-set `Z_\chi := \{\omega : S_\chi(\omega) = 0\}` defines a single
66	merged equivalence class; characters outside `Z_\chi` are singletons.
67	The Galois-orbit length distribution on equivalence classes is the
68	non-commutative-arithmetic invariant probed by D48: it is **statistically
69	indistinguishable from a random density-`|P_N|` subset** of `G` across
70	14 tested moduli (`|z(n_\mathrm{zero})| \leq 1.1` everywhere).
71

1274	primes (via the dynamical zeta function), then use Ruelle / Pollicott

**Question:** Define a dynamical system whose periodic orbits encode
primes (via the dynamical zeta function), then use Ruelle / Pollicott
results on exponential mixing to extract π(x).

**Why frontier:** the dynamical zeta function `ζ_φ(s) = exp(Σ Z_n s^n /n)`

correlations — maybe the analogous decay for "natural" Anosov flows
admits polylog extraction.

88	### A3 — Spectral primality test via custom self-adjoint operator
89	
90	**Question:** Build a self-adjoint operator T on a polylog-dim Hilbert
91	space such that the largest eigenvalue of T (or its sign, or its
92	parity) decides primality of the index n.
93	
94	**Why frontier:** if the operator's eigenvalue gap is Ω(1) and its
95	matrix entries are TC⁰-computable, then the dominant eigenvalue is
96	TC⁰-computable via power iteration → primality is in TC⁰.
97	
98	**Cross-domain ingredient:** spectral graph theory + representation
99	theory. Use the Cayley graph of (Z/nZ)* with respect to small generators
100	as a candidate graph. Or: use the regular representation of S_n with a
101	specific generator picked to encode primality.
102	
103	**Concrete first step:** for n in [2..50], build the Cayley graph of
104	(Z/nZ)* with generator set {2, 3, 5}. Compute its Laplacian spectrum.
105	Is there a spectral feature (eigenvalue gap, second eigenvalue, etc.)
106	that correlates with primality of n? Does the correlation persist for
107	n ∈ [50..200]?
108	
109	**Failure profile:** the spectrum is uniformly random across primes
110	and composites; or the spectral feature exists but is not TC⁰-computable.
111	
112	**Budget:** 3-5 sessions (this one is genuinely speculative).

114	### A4 — Bounded-arithmetic provability of a TC⁰ primality witness
115	
116	**Question:** Buss's theory `S^1_2` Σ^b_1-defines exactly the polynomial-
117	time functions, with witnessing: `S^1_2 ⊢ ∀x ∃y φ(x,y)` (φ ∈ Σ^b_1)
118	gives a polytime-computable witness. The Cook-Nguyen 2010 theory
119	`VTC^0` is the analogous theory for the complexity class TC^0. Question:
120	is there a Σ^B_1-statement φ(x) such that `VTC^0 ⊢ ∀x. (x ∈ PRIMES ↔ φ(x))`
121	would imply PRIMES ∈ TC^0? Equivalently: identify the precise
122	*proof-complexity* statement whose unprovability is the obstruction.
123	
124	**Why frontier:** the proof-complexity / circuit-complexity duality is
125	a separate barrier from the explicit-circuit-construction barrier the
126	project has been working on. A cleanly-stated `VTC^0`-provability
127	question is a publishable technical result on its own (Krajicek 2019
128	chapter on PRIMES is silent about VTC^0). Either we identify φ and
129	prove its `VTC^0`-provability (A-grade: PRIMES in TC^0), or we identify
130	φ and prove its `VTC^0`-unprovability via a Razborov-Rudich /
131	proof-complexity-natural-proofs barrier (B-grade: structural negative
132	result complementary to E5.3).
133	
134	**Cross-domain ingredient:** bounded arithmetic (Buss `S^1_2`), Cook-
135	Nguyen `VTC^0` and `VNC^1`, Σ^B_1 / Π^B_1 hierarchy, witnessing theorems.
136	This is **logic / proof-complexity**, not circuit complexity directly —
137	the project has not used it.
138	
139	**Concrete first step:** Read Cook-Nguyen 2010 §9 (theory `VTC^0`).
140	Write down the Σ^B_1 sentence φ_AKS that is the natural translation
141	of the AKS correctness proof. Verify (informally, on paper) that

### A3 — Spectral primality test via custom self-adjoint operator

**Question:** Build a self-adjoint operator T on a polylog-dim Hilbert
space such that the largest eigenvalue of T (or its sign, or its
parity) decides primality of the index n.

**Why frontier:** if the operator's eigenvalue gap is Ω(1) and its
matrix entries are TC⁰-computable, then the dominant eigenvalue is
TC⁰-computable via power iteration → primality is in TC⁰.

**Cross-domain ingredient:** spectral graph theory + representation
theory. Use the Cayley graph of (Z/nZ)* with respect to small generators
as a candidate graph. Or: use the regular representation of S_n with a
specific generator picked to encode primality.

**Concrete first step:** for n in [2..50], build the Cayley graph of
(Z/nZ)* with generator set {2, 3, 5}. Compute its Laplacian spectrum.
Is there a spectral feature (eigenvalue gap, second eigenvalue, etc.)
that correlates with primality of n? Does the correlation persist for
n ∈ [50..200]?

**Failure profile:** the spectrum is uniformly random across primes
and composites; or the spectral feature exists but is not TC⁰-computable.

**Budget:** 3-5 sessions (this one is genuinely speculative).

### A4 — Bounded-arithmetic provability of a TC⁰ primality witness

**Question:** Buss's theory `S^1_2` Σ^b_1-defines exactly the polynomial-
time functions, with witnessing: `S^1_2 ⊢ ∀x ∃y φ(x,y)` (φ ∈ Σ^b_1)
gives a polytime-computable witness. The Cook-Nguyen 2010 theory
`VTC^0` is the analogous theory for the complexity class TC^0. Question:
is there a Σ^B_1-statement φ(x) such that `VTC^0 ⊢ ∀x. (x ∈ PRIMES ↔ φ(x))`
would imply PRIMES ∈ TC^0? Equivalently: identify the precise
*proof-complexity* statement whose unprovability is the obstruction.

**Why frontier:** the proof-complexity / circuit-complexity duality is
a separate barrier from the explicit-circuit-construction barrier the
project has been working on. A cleanly-stated `VTC^0`-provability
question is a publishable technical result on its own (Krajicek 2019
chapter on PRIMES is silent about VTC^0). Either we identify φ and
prove its `VTC^0`-provability (A-grade: PRIMES in TC^0), or we identify
φ and prove its `VTC^0`-unprovability via a Razborov-Rudich /
proof-complexity-natural-proofs barrier (B-grade: structural negative
result complementary to E5.3).

**Cross-domain ingredient:** bounded arithmetic (Buss `S^1_2`), Cook-
Nguyen `VTC^0` and `VNC^1`, Σ^B_1 / Π^B_1 hierarchy, witnessing theorems.
This is **logic / proof-complexity**, not circuit complexity directly —
the project has not used it.

**Concrete first step:** Read Cook-Nguyen 2010 §9 (theory `VTC^0`).
Write down the Σ^B_1 sentence φ_AKS that is the natural translation
of the AKS correctness proof. Verify (informally, on paper) that
`VTC^0 ⊢ φ_AKS` would suffice — i.e., that Σ^B_1-witnessing for VTC^0
extracts a uniform TC^0 circuit from the proof. Then identify the
SPECIFIC subclaim of the AKS proof (likely "Σ Λ(p^k) ≥ x/log x for
some small range" or the cyclotomic factorisation step) whose
VTC^0-provability is the bottleneck.

**Failure profile (E):** the natural witness sentence φ_AKS reduces
to growing-dim MPOW in `VTC^0` (E5.3) and inherits its open status —
the formal-logic frame doesn't help. **(I):** the witness sentence is
unprovable in `VTC^0` by a proof-complexity natural-proofs / pseudorandom
function obstruction (e.g., Krajicek's witnessing barriers). **(INC):**
no clean Σ^B_1 sentence captures primality without circular reference
to AKS-style modular powering.

**A-grade success:** identify the precise φ + prove `VTC^0 ⊢ φ` ⇒
PRIMES ∈ TC^0, AND make non-trivial progress on whether `VTC^0 ⊢ φ`
holds (positive: TC^0 algorithm; negative: a new proof-complexity
barrier). **B-grade success:** identify φ but the provability is
equivalent to an existing closed barrier (E5.3, E5.8) — adds a new
"logical face" to the existing wall but no new bound.

**Cross-domain refs:**
- Buss 1986 thesis "Bounded Arithmetic"
  https://www.math.ucsd.edu/~sbuss/ResearchWeb/PhDThesis/index.html
- Cook-Nguyen 2010 "Logical Foundations of Proof Complexity"
  https://www.cs.toronto.edu/~sacook/  (book draft online)
- Krajicek 2019 "Proof Complexity" (Cambridge), chapters 5, 11
- Wikipedia: Bounded Arithmetic
  https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bounded_arithmetic

**Budget:** 2-3 sessions (heavy reading session 1, formalisation
session 2, attempt at provability/unprovability session 3).

553	`pi(N; q, a)` for `q ≤ Q*(N) ≈ N^{0.21}`, so the C2 spectral compression
554	barrier is the same object as the E1.5 / T6 saturation barrier viewed

559	follow-on conjecture `sigma_chi^2 ~ |L(1, chi)|^2` is REFUTED. Per-block

569	[B-grade per S167 verification, demoted from A]:**
570	S148's empirical "K-formula" `sum sigma^2 ≈ K · N / (p log²N)` is now
571	**proved analytically** for the primary subspace content. The exact result:
572	
573	> **Theorem (S166).** For W=2, N = 2^d, the L² energy of chi_P in the
574	> additive-Fourier subspace V_p^prim ⊕ V_{2p}^prim is
575	>
576	>   `E(p, N) = (2 (pi(N) - O(1))²) / ((p-1) N) + O(p · Var(p, N) / N)`
577	>
578	> where Var(p, N) = sum_{a coprime to p} (pi(N; p, a) - pi(N)/(p-1))² is
579	> the Gallagher PNT-in-AP variance. Equivalently:
580	>
581	>   `K(p, N) = E(p, N) · p log²N / N → 2p/(p-1) as N → ∞`,
582	>
583	> with finite-N correction `(pi(N) log N / N)²` (≈ 1.18 at d=20).
584	
585	Verified at 25 cells `(d, p) ∈ {14, 16, 18, 20, 22} × {3, 5, 7, 11, 13}`,
586	ratio empirical/predicted ∈ [0.992, 1.000] (max deviation 0.8%, shrinking
587	as N grows). **Proof:** Dirichlet character orthogonality + Ramanujan
588	sum identity `c_p(k) = mu(p) = -1` (k coprime to p prime) and
589	`c_{2p}(k) = mu(2p) = +1` (k coprime to 2p, p odd) give |S_q^k|² ≈
590	pi(N)²/(p-1)² for the additive-Fourier coefficient at k coprime to q.
591	Sum over (p-1) coprime k's per q ∈ {p, 2p}, divide by N, yields the
592	formula.
593

595	**Ramanujan-sum / principal-character quantity**, NOT a Gallagher
596	variance. The Gallagher variance enters only in the sub-leading
597	remainder `R(p, N)`. The empirical K ≈ 3.86 in S148 was a *p-dependent*
598	quantity averaged across (d, p); the asymptotic K = 2p/(p-1) is exact.
599	
600	**SVD spike-block leakage (ancillary):** the empirical SVD spike block
601	sum (top phi(p) sigma² after the rank-1 mean) **exceeds** E(p, N) by a
602	"leakage" that shrinks with N (e.g., p=3: 18% leakage at d=14 → 4% at
603	d=20) and grows with p at fixed N (4% / 15% / 38% at p=3 / 5 / 7, d=20).
604	Asymptotically, leakage → 0 and SVD block → E(p, N).
605	
606	**Implication:** the spike-block sigma² is now **explicitly identified**
607	as a class-number-style principal-character quantity, removing both the
608	S82 |L(1,chi)|² claim and the S148 Gallagher-variance claim as the
609	*main term*. The C-circular failure stands: computing E(p, N) requires
610	pi(N), and the remainder requires Gallagher 2nd-moment data.
611	
612	See `experiments/constructions/spike_gallagher_proof/`.
613

615	theorem extends UNIFORMLY to all squarefree q ≥ 2 with the SAME
616	constant of proportionality.
617	
618	> **Theorem (S168).** For every squarefree integer q ≥ 2, with
619	> r(q) = number of distinct primes dividing q,
620	>
621	>   `E(q, N) = ‖P_{V_q^prim} chi_P‖² / N
622	>           = μ(q)² · (π(N) − r(q))² / (φ(q) N) + R(q, N)`,
623	>
624	>   `|R(q, N)| ≤ q · Var(q, N) / N + O(r(q)² / N)`.
625	>
626	> **Corollary (μ-vanishing):** for non-squarefree q, the main term is
627	> identically zero. **Corollary (additivity):** total chi_P energy in
628	> ⊕_{q sqf, q ≤ Q*} V_q^prim is `(π(N)²/N) · Σ_{q sqf ≤ Q*} 1/φ(q)
629	> ~ A · π(N)² log Q* / N` with `A → 1` (Selberg-Delange).

638	at d=18 for q ∈ {4, 8, 9, 12, ..., 50}, E_emp ≤ q·Var/N strictly with

642	matches `Σ_{sqf q ≤ Q*} φ(q) ~ (3/π²) Q*²`, then `Q* ~ N^{0.21}`, hence

    rng: np.random.Generator,

    Toeplitz/Hankel of size N (after standardising), return eigenvalues/sqrt(N)."""
    raw = rng.binomial(1, p, size=n_seq).astype(np.float64)
    p_var = p * (1.0 - p)
    return normalised_eigenvalues(raw, N, kind, p_mean=p, p_var=p_var)

    rng: np.random.Generator,
    chi_seq: np.ndarray,
    N: int,

"""
D3 attack: free-probability via Bryc-Dembo-Jiang Toeplitz/Hankel LSD on chi_P.

We embed the prime indicator chi_P[1..2N] as the data sequence underlying
real symmetric Toeplitz T_N (T_{ij} = chi_P(|i-j|+1) for 0<=i,j<N) and
real symmetric Hankel H_N (H_{ij} = chi_P(i+j+1)) matrices.

After centring (chi_P - p_N) and normalising entries to unit variance, the
classical Bryc-Dembo-Jiang 2006 (Ann. Probab. 34, 1-38) theorem says that for
i.i.d. mean-0 variance-1 entries, eigenvalues / sqrt(N) converge to universal
distributions gamma_T (Toeplitz) and gamma_H (Hankel) of unbounded support
with even moments
    m_{2k} = sum over "good" link/non-crossing pair partitions (Eulerian
             number combinatorics; see BDJ 2006 + Hammond-Miller 2005).
The first numerical values are
    Toeplitz:  m_2 = 1, m_4 = 8/3, m_6 ~ 11.67 (BDJ 2006)
    Hankel:    m_2 = 1, m_4 = 2, m_6 ~ 11
For Gaussian (semicircle is wrong here - that's Wigner) reference, we use
Bernoulli-matched-density NULL (i.i.d. Bern(p) - p, divided by sqrt(p(1-p))),
which is the exact 1st-2-moment-matched chi_P null.

Falsifier (pre-registered):
- Mode I (A-grade): chi_P empirical moment m_k differs from matched-Bernoulli
  null by >= 3 sigma at any k in {2, 4, 6, 8} for at least 2 distinct N >=
  1500, in the SAME direction for both T and H.
- Mode E (B-grade orthogonality): chi_P moments match null within +-2 sigma
  across all N tested. -> 15th orthogonal pseudorandomness category.
- Mode INC: variance dominates signal at the scales tested.

Cross-domain ingredient: Bryc-Dembo-Jiang 2006 universal Toeplitz/Hankel LSD,
real symmetric variant; Hammond-Miller 2005 Toeplitz "good" pair partition
moment expansion. Channelled mathematician: Bryc / Voiculescu (operator-
algebra free probability rigour).
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import json
import math
import os
import time
from dataclasses import dataclass, asdict
from typing import Any

import numpy as np


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Sieve and chi_P sequence
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
def sieve_chi_p(M: int) -> np.ndarray:
    """Return chi_P[0..M-1] with chi_P[k] = 1 iff k+1 is prime, else 0.

    So chi_P sequence is indexed from 1 (i.e. chi_P at index 0 represents n=1).
    Convention: 1 is NOT prime.
    """
    sieve = np.ones(M + 1, dtype=bool)
    sieve[0] = sieve[1] = False
    for i in range(2, int(math.isqrt(M)) + 1):
        if sieve[i]:
            sieve[i * i :: i] = False
    return sieve[1 : M + 1].astype(np.float64)


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Matrix builders
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
def build_toeplitz(seq: np.ndarray, N: int) -> np.ndarray:
    """Symmetric Toeplitz, T_{ij} = seq[|i-j|], i,j in [0,N).

    Requires len(seq) >= N.
    """
    idx = np.abs(np.arange(N)[:, None] - np.arange(N)[None, :])
    return seq[idx]


def build_hankel(seq: np.ndarray, N: int) -> np.ndarray:
    """Symmetric Hankel, H_{ij} = seq[i+j], i,j in [0,N).

    Requires len(seq) >= 2N - 1.
    """
    idx = np.arange(N)[:, None] + np.arange(N)[None, :]
    return seq[idx]


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Spectral-moment computation
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
def normalised_eigenvalues(
    seq: np.ndarray,
    N: int,
    kind: str,
    p_mean: float,
    p_var: float,
) -> np.ndarray:
    """Centre `seq` by p_mean, scale to unit-variance, build matrix, return
    eigenvalues divided by sqrt(N) (BDJ scaling)."""
    if p_var <= 0:
        raise ValueError(f"non-positive entry variance p_var={p_var}")
    s_centered = (seq - p_mean) / math.sqrt(p_var)
    if kind == "T":
        M = build_toeplitz(s_centered, N)
    elif kind == "H":
        M = build_hankel(s_centered, N)
    else:
        raise ValueError(kind)
    w = np.linalg.eigvalsh(M)
    return w / math.sqrt(N)


def spectral_moments(eigs: np.ndarray, ks: tuple[int, ...]) -> dict[int, float]:
    """Empirical even moments m_k = mean_{lambda} lambda^k."""
    out: dict[int, float] = {}
    for k in ks:
        out[k] = float(np.mean(eigs ** k))
    return out


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Null: i.i.d. Bernoulli(p) matched-density, same matrix-type
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
def bernoulli_null_eigs(
    rng: np.random.Generator,
    N: int,
    kind: str,
    p: float,
    n_seq: int,
) -> np.ndarray:
    """Sample i.i.d. Bern(p) - p sequence of length n_seq, build Toeplitz/Hankel
    of size N (after standardising to unit variance), return eigenvalues/sqrt(N).
    """
    raw = rng.binomial(1, p, size=n_seq).astype(np.float64)
    # The Toeplitz/Hankel kernels here use (raw - p) / sqrt(p(1-p)),
    # i.e. zero mean unit variance. Match the chi_P normalisation exactly.
    p_var = p * (1.0 - p)
    return normalised_eigenvalues(raw, N, kind, p_mean=p, p_var=p_var)


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Sweep
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
@dataclass
class CellResult:
    N: int
    kind: str  # "T" or "H"
    p_N: float
    chi_moments: dict[int, float]
    null_mean: dict[int, float]
    null_std: dict[int, float]
    z: dict[int, float]
    null_trials: int
    seconds: float


def run_cell(
    chi_seq_full: np.ndarray,
    N: int,
    kind: str,
    p_N: float,
    moments: tuple[int, ...],
    null_trials: int,
    rng: np.random.Generator,
) -> CellResult:
    t0 = time.time()
    n_seq_needed = N if kind == "T" else 2 * N - 1
    chi_eigs = normalised_eigenvalues(
        chi_seq_full[:n_seq_needed], N, kind, p_mean=p_N, p_var=p_N * (1.0 - p_N)
    )
    chi_m = spectral_moments(chi_eigs, moments)

    null_arrays = {k: np.empty(null_trials, dtype=np.float64) for k in moments}
    for t in range(null_trials):
        e = bernoulli_null_eigs(rng, N, kind, p_N, n_seq_needed)
        m = spectral_moments(e, moments)
        for k in moments:
            null_arrays[k][t] = m[k]

    null_mean = {k: float(null_arrays[k].mean()) for k in moments}
    null_std = {k: float(null_arrays[k].std(ddof=1)) for k in moments}
    z = {
        k: (chi_m[k] - null_mean[k]) / null_std[k] if null_std[k] > 0 else 0.0
        for k in moments
    }
    return CellResult(
        N=N,
        kind=kind,
        p_N=p_N,
        chi_moments=chi_m,
        null_mean=null_mean,
        null_std=null_std,
        z=z,
        null_trials=null_trials,
        seconds=time.time() - t0,
    )


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Main
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
def main() -> int:
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument(
        "--Ns",
        type=int,
        nargs="+",
        default=[500, 1000, 2000, 3500],
        help="matrix sizes",
    )
    ap.add_argument("--moments", type=int, nargs="+", default=[2, 4, 6, 8])
    ap.add_argument("--null-trials", type=int, default=50)
    ap.add_argument("--seed", type=int, default=20260428)
    ap.add_argument("--out-json", type=str, default=None)
    args = ap.parse_args()

    Ns = sorted(set(args.Ns))
    rng = np.random.default_rng(args.seed)
    moments = tuple(args.moments)

    # Pre-sieve enough chi_P
    M_needed = 2 * max(Ns) + 5
    chi_full = sieve_chi_p(M_needed)
    print(f"[sieve] generated chi_P on [1, {M_needed}], "
          f"prime count = {int(chi_full.sum())}")

    cells: list[CellResult] = []
    for N in Ns:
        n_seq = 2 * N - 1
        p_N = float(chi_full[:n_seq].mean())
        for kind in ("T", "H"):
            print(f"[cell] N={N} kind={kind} p_N={p_N:.6f} ... ", flush=True)
            r = run_cell(
                chi_full, N, kind, p_N, moments, args.null_trials, rng
            )
            cells.append(r)
            zs = ", ".join(f"m{k}: z={r.z[k]:+.2f}" for k in moments)
            print(f"   chi: {r.chi_moments}\n   null mean: {r.null_mean}\n"
                  f"   null std:  {r.null_std}\n   {zs}\n   "
                  f"({r.seconds:.1f}s)")

    # Summarize: max|z| across cells per moment k
    max_z = {k: 0.0 for k in moments}
    arg_max_z: dict[int, str] = {}
    for r in cells:
        for k in moments:
            if abs(r.z[k]) > max_z[k]:
                max_z[k] = abs(r.z[k])
                arg_max_z[k] = f"N={r.N} kind={r.kind}"

    print()
    print("=" * 60)
    print("Summary: max |z| per moment across all cells")
    for k in moments:
        print(f"  m_{k}: max |z| = {max_z[k]:.2f} at {arg_max_z[k]}")

    # Bonferroni:
    n_tests = len(cells) * len(moments)
    print(f"  total cells x moments = {n_tests}; Bonferroni-3sigma is "
          f"~ {3 + math.sqrt(2 * math.log(n_tests)):.2f}-sigma raw threshold")

    out = {
        "config": vars(args),
        "cells": [asdict(c) for c in cells],
        "summary": {
            "max_z_per_moment": max_z,
            "arg_max_z_per_moment": arg_max_z,
            "n_cells_x_moments": n_tests,
        },
    }

    out_json = args.out_json or os.path.join(
        os.path.dirname(__file__),
        "bdj_toeplitz_hankel_chi_p_results.json",
    )
    # Convert int-keyed dicts to str for JSON
    def _stringify(o: Any) -> Any:
        if isinstance(o, dict):
            return {str(k): _stringify(v) for k, v in o.items()}
        if isinstance(o, list):
            return [_stringify(v) for v in o]
        return o

    with open(out_json, "w") as f:
        json.dump(_stringify(out), f, indent=2, default=str)
    print(f"\nWrote {out_json}")
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    raise SystemExit(main())

D3 attack: free-probability via Bryc-Dembo-Jiang Toeplitz/Hankel LSD on chi_P.

We embed the prime indicator chi_P[1..2N] as the data sequence underlying
real symmetric Toeplitz T_N (T_{ij} = chi_P(|i-j|+1) for 0<=i,j<N) and
real symmetric Hankel H_N (H_{ij} = chi_P(i+j+1)) matrices.

After centring (chi_P - p_N) and normalising entries to unit variance, the
classical Bryc-Dembo-Jiang 2006 (Ann. Probab. 34, 1-38) theorem says that for
i.i.d. mean-0 variance-1 entries, eigenvalues / sqrt(N) converge to universal
distributions gamma_T (Toeplitz) and gamma_H (Hankel) of unbounded support
with even moments
    m_{2k} = sum over "good" link/non-crossing pair partitions (Eulerian
             number combinatorics; see BDJ 2006 + Hammond-Miller 2005).
The first numerical values are
    Toeplitz:  m_2 = 1, m_4 = 8/3, m_6 ~ 11.67 (BDJ 2006)
    Hankel:    m_2 = 1, m_4 = 2, m_6 ~ 11
For Gaussian (semicircle is wrong here - that's Wigner) reference, we use
Bernoulli-matched-density NULL (i.i.d. Bern(p) - p, divided by sqrt(p(1-p))),
which is the exact 1st-2-moment-matched chi_P null.

Falsifier (pre-registered):
- Mode I (A-grade): chi_P empirical moment m_k differs from matched-Bernoulli
  null by >= 3 sigma at any k in {2, 4, 6, 8} for at least 2 distinct N >=
  1500, in the SAME direction for both T and H.
- Mode E (B-grade orthogonality): chi_P moments match null within +-2 sigma
  across all N tested. -> 15th orthogonal pseudorandomness category.
- Mode INC: variance dominates signal at the scales tested.

Cross-domain ingredient: Bryc-Dembo-Jiang 2006 universal Toeplitz/Hankel LSD,
real symmetric variant; Hammond-Miller 2005 Toeplitz "good" pair partition
moment expansion. Channelled mathematician: Bryc / Voiculescu (operator-
algebra free probability rigour).
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import json
import math
import os
import time
from dataclasses import dataclass, asdict
from typing import Any

import numpy as np


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Sieve and chi_P sequence
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
def sieve_chi_p(M: int) -> np.ndarray:
    """Return chi_P[0..M-1] with chi_P[k] = 1 iff k+1 is prime, else 0.

    So chi_P sequence is indexed from 1 (i.e. chi_P at index 0 represents n=1).
    Convention: 1 is NOT prime.
    """
    sieve = np.ones(M + 1, dtype=bool)
    sieve[0] = sieve[1] = False
    for i in range(2, int(math.isqrt(M)) + 1):
        if sieve[i]:
            sieve[i * i :: i] = False
    return sieve[1 : M + 1].astype(np.float64)


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Matrix builders
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
def build_toeplitz(seq: np.ndarray, N: int) -> np.ndarray:
    """Symmetric Toeplitz, T_{ij} = seq[|i-j|], i,j in [0,N).

    Requires len(seq) >= N.
    """
    idx = np.abs(np.arange(N)[:, None] - np.arange(N)[None, :])
    return seq[idx]


def build_hankel(seq: np.ndarray, N: int) -> np.ndarray:
    """Symmetric Hankel, H_{ij} = seq[i+j], i,j in [0,N).

    Requires len(seq) >= 2N - 1.
    """
    idx = np.arange(N)[:, None] + np.arange(N)[None, :]
    return seq[idx]


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Spectral-moment computation
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
def normalised_eigenvalues(
    seq: np.ndarray,
    N: int,
    kind: str,
    p_mean: float,
    p_var: float,
) -> np.ndarray:
    """Centre `seq` by p_mean, scale to unit-variance, build matrix, return
    eigenvalues divided by sqrt(N) (BDJ scaling)."""
    if p_var <= 0:
        raise ValueError(f"non-positive entry variance p_var={p_var}")
    s_centered = (seq - p_mean) / math.sqrt(p_var)
    if kind == "T":
        M = build_toeplitz(s_centered, N)
    elif kind == "H":
        M = build_hankel(s_centered, N)
    else:
        raise ValueError(kind)
    w = np.linalg.eigvalsh(M)
    return w / math.sqrt(N)


def spectral_moments(eigs: np.ndarray, ks: tuple[int, ...]) -> dict[int, float]:
    """Empirical even moments m_k = mean_{lambda} lambda^k."""
    out: dict[int, float] = {}
    for k in ks:
        out[k] = float(np.mean(eigs ** k))
    return out


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Nulls: (B1) i.i.d. Bernoulli(p) matched-density, (B2) random permutation
# of chi_P (matches multiset of values exactly), same matrix-type
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
def bernoulli_null_eigs(
    rng: np.random.Generator,
    N: int,
    kind: str,
    p: float,
    n_seq: int,
) -> np.ndarray:
    """B1: sample i.i.d. Bern(p) - p sequence of length n_seq, build
    Toeplitz/Hankel of size N (after standardising), return eigenvalues/sqrt(N)."""
    raw = rng.binomial(1, p, size=n_seq).astype(np.float64)
    p_var = p * (1.0 - p)
    return normalised_eigenvalues(raw, N, kind, p_mean=p, p_var=p_var)


def permutation_null_eigs(
    rng: np.random.Generator,
    chi_seq: np.ndarray,
    N: int,
    kind: str,
    p: float,
) -> np.ndarray:
    """B2: random permutation of chi_seq; matches MULTISET of values exactly.
    Any deviation from chi_P here is from positional order (= prime arithmetic
    structure), not from value-distribution mismatch."""
    perm = rng.permutation(chi_seq)
    p_var = p * (1.0 - p)
    return normalised_eigenvalues(perm, N, kind, p_mean=p, p_var=p_var)


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Sweep
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
@dataclass
class CellResult:
    N: int
    kind: str  # "T" or "H"
    p_N: float
    chi_moments: dict[int, float]
    null_mean: dict[int, float]
    null_std: dict[int, float]
    z: dict[int, float]
    null_trials: int
    seconds: float


def run_cell(
    chi_seq_full: np.ndarray,
    N: int,
    kind: str,
    p_N: float,
    moments: tuple[int, ...],
    null_trials: int,
    rng: np.random.Generator,
) -> CellResult:
    t0 = time.time()
    n_seq_needed = N if kind == "T" else 2 * N - 1
    chi_eigs = normalised_eigenvalues(
        chi_seq_full[:n_seq_needed], N, kind, p_mean=p_N, p_var=p_N * (1.0 - p_N)
    )
    chi_m = spectral_moments(chi_eigs, moments)

    null_arrays = {k: np.empty(null_trials, dtype=np.float64) for k in moments}
    for t in range(null_trials):
        e = bernoulli_null_eigs(rng, N, kind, p_N, n_seq_needed)
        m = spectral_moments(e, moments)
        for k in moments:
            null_arrays[k][t] = m[k]

    null_mean = {k: float(null_arrays[k].mean()) for k in moments}
    null_std = {k: float(null_arrays[k].std(ddof=1)) for k in moments}
    z = {
        k: (chi_m[k] - null_mean[k]) / null_std[k] if null_std[k] > 0 else 0.0
        for k in moments
    }
    return CellResult(
        N=N,
        kind=kind,
        p_N=p_N,
        chi_moments=chi_m,
        null_mean=null_mean,
        null_std=null_std,
        z=z,
        null_trials=null_trials,
        seconds=time.time() - t0,
    )


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Main
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
def main() -> int:
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument(
        "--Ns",
        type=int,
        nargs="+",
        default=[500, 1000, 2000, 3500],
        help="matrix sizes",
    )
    ap.add_argument("--moments", type=int, nargs="+", default=[2, 4, 6, 8])
    ap.add_argument("--null-trials", type=int, default=50)
    ap.add_argument("--seed", type=int, default=20260428)
    ap.add_argument("--out-json", type=str, default=None)
    args = ap.parse_args()

    Ns = sorted(set(args.Ns))
    rng = np.random.default_rng(args.seed)
    moments = tuple(args.moments)

    # Pre-sieve enough chi_P
    M_needed = 2 * max(Ns) + 5
    chi_full = sieve_chi_p(M_needed)
    print(f"[sieve] generated chi_P on [1, {M_needed}], "
          f"prime count = {int(chi_full.sum())}")

    cells: list[CellResult] = []
    for N in Ns:
        n_seq = 2 * N - 1
        p_N = float(chi_full[:n_seq].mean())
        for kind in ("T", "H"):
            print(f"[cell] N={N} kind={kind} p_N={p_N:.6f} ... ", flush=True)
            r = run_cell(
                chi_full, N, kind, p_N, moments, args.null_trials, rng
            )
            cells.append(r)
            zs = ", ".join(f"m{k}: z={r.z[k]:+.2f}" for k in moments)
            print(f"   chi: {r.chi_moments}\n   null mean: {r.null_mean}\n"
                  f"   null std:  {r.null_std}\n   {zs}\n   "
                  f"({r.seconds:.1f}s)")

    # Summarize: max|z| across cells per moment k
    max_z = {k: 0.0 for k in moments}
    arg_max_z: dict[int, str] = {}
    for r in cells:
        for k in moments:
            if abs(r.z[k]) > max_z[k]:
                max_z[k] = abs(r.z[k])
                arg_max_z[k] = f"N={r.N} kind={r.kind}"

    print()
    print("=" * 60)
    print("Summary: max |z| per moment across all cells")
    for k in moments:
        print(f"  m_{k}: max |z| = {max_z[k]:.2f} at {arg_max_z[k]}")

    # Bonferroni:
    n_tests = len(cells) * len(moments)
    print(f"  total cells x moments = {n_tests}; Bonferroni-3sigma is "
          f"~ {3 + math.sqrt(2 * math.log(n_tests)):.2f}-sigma raw threshold")

    out = {
        "config": vars(args),
        "cells": [asdict(c) for c in cells],
        "summary": {
            "max_z_per_moment": max_z,
            "arg_max_z_per_moment": arg_max_z,
            "n_cells_x_moments": n_tests,
        },
    }

    out_json = args.out_json or os.path.join(
        os.path.dirname(__file__),
        "bdj_toeplitz_hankel_chi_p_results.json",
    )
    # Convert int-keyed dicts to str for JSON
    def _stringify(o: Any) -> Any:
        if isinstance(o, dict):
            return {str(k): _stringify(v) for k, v in o.items()}
        if isinstance(o, list):
            return [_stringify(v) for v in o]
        return o

    with open(out_json, "w") as f:
        json.dump(_stringify(out), f, indent=2, default=str)
    print(f"\nWrote {out_json}")
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    raise SystemExit(main())

"""
D3 attack: free-probability via Bryc-Dembo-Jiang Toeplitz/Hankel LSD on chi_P.

We embed the prime indicator chi_P[1..2N] as the data sequence underlying
real symmetric Toeplitz T_N (T_{ij} = chi_P(|i-j|+1) for 0<=i,j<N) and
real symmetric Hankel H_N (H_{ij} = chi_P(i+j+1)) matrices.

After centring (chi_P - p_N) and normalising entries to unit variance, the
classical Bryc-Dembo-Jiang 2006 (Ann. Probab. 34, 1-38) theorem says that for
i.i.d. mean-0 variance-1 entries, eigenvalues / sqrt(N) converge to universal
distributions gamma_T (Toeplitz) and gamma_H (Hankel) of unbounded support
with even moments
    m_{2k} = sum over "good" link/non-crossing pair partitions (Eulerian
             number combinatorics; see BDJ 2006 + Hammond-Miller 2005).
The first numerical values are
    Toeplitz:  m_2 = 1, m_4 = 8/3, m_6 ~ 11.67 (BDJ 2006)
    Hankel:    m_2 = 1, m_4 = 2, m_6 ~ 11
For Gaussian (semicircle is wrong here - that's Wigner) reference, we use
Bernoulli-matched-density NULL (i.i.d. Bern(p) - p, divided by sqrt(p(1-p))),
which is the exact 1st-2-moment-matched chi_P null.

Falsifier (pre-registered):
- Mode I (A-grade): chi_P empirical moment m_k differs from matched-Bernoulli
  null by >= 3 sigma at any k in {2, 4, 6, 8} for at least 2 distinct N >=
  1500, in the SAME direction for both T and H.
- Mode E (B-grade orthogonality): chi_P moments match null within +-2 sigma
  across all N tested. -> 15th orthogonal pseudorandomness category.
- Mode INC: variance dominates signal at the scales tested.

Cross-domain ingredient: Bryc-Dembo-Jiang 2006 universal Toeplitz/Hankel LSD,
real symmetric variant; Hammond-Miller 2005 Toeplitz "good" pair partition
moment expansion. Channelled mathematician: Bryc / Voiculescu (operator-
algebra free probability rigour).
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import json
import math
import os
import time
from dataclasses import dataclass, asdict
from typing import Any

import numpy as np


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Sieve and chi_P sequence
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
def sieve_chi_p(M: int) -> np.ndarray:
    """Return chi_P[0..M-1] with chi_P[k] = 1 iff k+1 is prime, else 0.

    So chi_P sequence is indexed from 1 (i.e. chi_P at index 0 represents n=1).
    Convention: 1 is NOT prime.
    """
    sieve = np.ones(M + 1, dtype=bool)
    sieve[0] = sieve[1] = False
    for i in range(2, int(math.isqrt(M)) + 1):
        if sieve[i]:
            sieve[i * i :: i] = False
    return sieve[1 : M + 1].astype(np.float64)


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Matrix builders
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
def build_toeplitz(seq: np.ndarray, N: int) -> np.ndarray:
    """Symmetric Toeplitz, T_{ij} = seq[|i-j|], i,j in [0,N).

    Requires len(seq) >= N.
    """
    idx = np.abs(np.arange(N)[:, None] - np.arange(N)[None, :])
    return seq[idx]


def build_hankel(seq: np.ndarray, N: int) -> np.ndarray:
    """Symmetric Hankel, H_{ij} = seq[i+j], i,j in [0,N).

    Requires len(seq) >= 2N - 1.
    """
    idx = np.arange(N)[:, None] + np.arange(N)[None, :]
    return seq[idx]


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Spectral-moment computation
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
def normalised_eigenvalues(
    seq: np.ndarray,
    N: int,
    kind: str,
    p_mean: float,
    p_var: float,
) -> np.ndarray:
    """Centre `seq` by p_mean, scale to unit-variance, build matrix, return
    eigenvalues divided by sqrt(N) (BDJ scaling)."""
    if p_var <= 0:
        raise ValueError(f"non-positive entry variance p_var={p_var}")
    s_centered = (seq - p_mean) / math.sqrt(p_var)
    if kind == "T":
        M = build_toeplitz(s_centered, N)
    elif kind == "H":
        M = build_hankel(s_centered, N)
    else:
        raise ValueError(kind)
    w = np.linalg.eigvalsh(M)
    return w / math.sqrt(N)


def spectral_moments(eigs: np.ndarray, ks: tuple[int, ...]) -> dict[int, float]:
    """Empirical even moments m_k = mean_{lambda} lambda^k."""
    out: dict[int, float] = {}
    for k in ks:
        out[k] = float(np.mean(eigs ** k))
    return out


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Nulls: (B1) i.i.d. Bernoulli(p) matched-density, (B2) random permutation
# of chi_P (matches multiset of values exactly), same matrix-type
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
def bernoulli_null_eigs(
    rng: np.random.Generator,
    N: int,
    kind: str,
    p: float,
    n_seq: int,
) -> np.ndarray:
    """B1: sample i.i.d. Bern(p) - p sequence of length n_seq, build
    Toeplitz/Hankel of size N (after standardising), return eigenvalues/sqrt(N)."""
    raw = rng.binomial(1, p, size=n_seq).astype(np.float64)
    p_var = p * (1.0 - p)
    return normalised_eigenvalues(raw, N, kind, p_mean=p, p_var=p_var)


def permutation_null_eigs(
    rng: np.random.Generator,
    chi_seq: np.ndarray,
    N: int,
    kind: str,
    p: float,
) -> np.ndarray:
    """B2: random permutation of chi_seq; matches MULTISET of values exactly.
    Any deviation from chi_P here is from positional order (= prime arithmetic
    structure), not from value-distribution mismatch."""
    perm = rng.permutation(chi_seq)
    p_var = p * (1.0 - p)
    return normalised_eigenvalues(perm, N, kind, p_mean=p, p_var=p_var)

# Sweep
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
@dataclass
class NullStats:
    mean: dict[int, float]
    std: dict[int, float]
    z: dict[int, float]
    trials: int


@dataclass

    N: int
    kind: str  # "T" or "H"
    p_N: float
    chi_moments: dict[int, float]
    bern: NullStats
    perm: NullStats
    chi_lambda_max: float
    chi_lambda_min: float
    seconds: float


def _null_stats(
    null_arrays: dict[int, np.ndarray],
    chi_m: dict[int, float],
    moments: tuple[int, ...],
    n_trials: int,
) -> NullStats:
    mean = {k: float(null_arrays[k].mean()) for k in moments}
    std = {k: float(null_arrays[k].std(ddof=1)) for k in moments}
    z = {
        k: (chi_m[k] - mean[k]) / std[k] if std[k] > 0 else 0.0
        for k in moments
    }
    return NullStats(mean=mean, std=std, z=z, trials=n_trials)


def run_cell(
    chi_seq_full: np.ndarray,
    N: int,
    kind: str,
    p_N: float,
    moments: tuple[int, ...],
    null_trials: int,
    rng: np.random.Generator,
) -> CellResult:
    t0 = time.time()
    n_seq_needed = N if kind == "T" else 2 * N - 1
    chi_seq_used = chi_seq_full[:n_seq_needed]
    chi_eigs = normalised_eigenvalues(

    )

    bern_arrays = {k: np.empty(null_trials, dtype=np.float64) for k in moments}
    perm_arrays = {k: np.empty(null_trials, dtype=np.float64) for k in moments}
    for t in range(null_trials):

        m_b = spectral_moments(e_b, moments)

            perm_arrays[k][t] = m_p[k]

    perm = _null_stats(perm_arrays, chi_m, moments, null_trials)

        N=N,
        kind=kind,
        p_N=p_N,
        chi_moments=chi_m,
        bern=bern,

        seconds=time.time() - t0,
    )

"""
D3 attack: free-probability via Bryc-Dembo-Jiang Toeplitz/Hankel LSD on chi_P.

We embed the prime indicator chi_P[1..2N] as the data sequence underlying
real symmetric Toeplitz T_N (T_{ij} = chi_P(|i-j|+1) for 0<=i,j<N) and
real symmetric Hankel H_N (H_{ij} = chi_P(i+j+1)) matrices.

After centring (chi_P - p_N) and normalising entries to unit variance, the
classical Bryc-Dembo-Jiang 2006 (Ann. Probab. 34, 1-38) theorem says that for
i.i.d. mean-0 variance-1 entries, eigenvalues / sqrt(N) converge to universal
distributions gamma_T (Toeplitz) and gamma_H (Hankel) of unbounded support
with even moments
    m_{2k} = sum over "good" link/non-crossing pair partitions (Eulerian
             number combinatorics; see BDJ 2006 + Hammond-Miller 2005).
The first numerical values are
    Toeplitz:  m_2 = 1, m_4 = 8/3, m_6 ~ 11.67 (BDJ 2006)
    Hankel:    m_2 = 1, m_4 = 2, m_6 ~ 11
For Gaussian (semicircle is wrong here - that's Wigner) reference, we use
Bernoulli-matched-density NULL (i.i.d. Bern(p) - p, divided by sqrt(p(1-p))),
which is the exact 1st-2-moment-matched chi_P null.

Falsifier (pre-registered):
- Mode I (A-grade): chi_P empirical moment m_k differs from matched-Bernoulli
  null by >= 3 sigma at any k in {2, 4, 6, 8} for at least 2 distinct N >=
  1500, in the SAME direction for both T and H.
- Mode E (B-grade orthogonality): chi_P moments match null within +-2 sigma
  across all N tested. -> 15th orthogonal pseudorandomness category.
- Mode INC: variance dominates signal at the scales tested.

Cross-domain ingredient: Bryc-Dembo-Jiang 2006 universal Toeplitz/Hankel LSD,
real symmetric variant; Hammond-Miller 2005 Toeplitz "good" pair partition
moment expansion. Channelled mathematician: Bryc / Voiculescu (operator-
algebra free probability rigour).
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import json
import math
import os
import time
from dataclasses import dataclass, asdict
from typing import Any

import numpy as np


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Sieve and chi_P sequence
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
def sieve_chi_p(M: int) -> np.ndarray:
    """Return chi_P[0..M-1] with chi_P[k] = 1 iff k+1 is prime, else 0.

    So chi_P sequence is indexed from 1 (i.e. chi_P at index 0 represents n=1).
    Convention: 1 is NOT prime.
    """
    sieve = np.ones(M + 1, dtype=bool)
    sieve[0] = sieve[1] = False
    for i in range(2, int(math.isqrt(M)) + 1):
        if sieve[i]:
            sieve[i * i :: i] = False
    return sieve[1 : M + 1].astype(np.float64)


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Matrix builders
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
def build_toeplitz(seq: np.ndarray, N: int) -> np.ndarray:
    """Symmetric Toeplitz, T_{ij} = seq[|i-j|], i,j in [0,N).

    Requires len(seq) >= N.
    """
    idx = np.abs(np.arange(N)[:, None] - np.arange(N)[None, :])
    return seq[idx]


def build_hankel(seq: np.ndarray, N: int) -> np.ndarray:
    """Symmetric Hankel, H_{ij} = seq[i+j], i,j in [0,N).

    Requires len(seq) >= 2N - 1.
    """
    idx = np.arange(N)[:, None] + np.arange(N)[None, :]
    return seq[idx]


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Spectral-moment computation
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
def normalised_eigenvalues(
    seq: np.ndarray,
    N: int,
    kind: str,
    p_mean: float,
    p_var: float,
) -> np.ndarray:
    """Centre `seq` by p_mean, scale to unit-variance, build matrix, return
    eigenvalues divided by sqrt(N) (BDJ scaling)."""
    if p_var <= 0:
        raise ValueError(f"non-positive entry variance p_var={p_var}")
    s_centered = (seq - p_mean) / math.sqrt(p_var)
    if kind == "T":
        M = build_toeplitz(s_centered, N)
    elif kind == "H":
        M = build_hankel(s_centered, N)
    else:
        raise ValueError(kind)
    w = np.linalg.eigvalsh(M)
    return w / math.sqrt(N)


def spectral_moments(eigs: np.ndarray, ks: tuple[int, ...]) -> dict[int, float]:
    """Empirical even moments m_k = mean_{lambda} lambda^k."""
    out: dict[int, float] = {}
    for k in ks:
        out[k] = float(np.mean(eigs ** k))
    return out

def bernoulli_null_eigs(

    raw = rng.binomial(1, p, size=n_seq).astype(np.float64)

    perm = rng.permutation(chi_seq)

distributions gamma_T (Toeplitz) and gamma_H (Hankel) of unbounded support

Bernoulli-matched-density NULL (i.i.d. Bern(p) - p, divided by sqrt(p(1-p))),
which is the exact 1st-2-moment-matched chi_P null.

  null by >= 3 sigma at any k in {2, 4, 6, 8} for at least 2 distinct N >=

  across all N tested. -> 15th orthogonal pseudorandomness category.
- Mode INC: variance dominates signal at the scales tested.

algebra free probability rigour).

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import json
import math
import os
import time
from dataclasses import dataclass, asdict
from typing import Any

import numpy as np


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Sieve and chi_P sequence
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
def sieve_chi_p(M: int) -> np.ndarray:
    """Return chi_P[0..M-1] with chi_P[k] = 1 iff k+1 is prime, else 0.

    So chi_P sequence is indexed from 1 (i.e. chi_P at index 0 represents n=1).
    Convention: 1 is NOT prime.
    """
    sieve = np.ones(M + 1, dtype=bool)
    sieve[0] = sieve[1] = False
    for i in range(2, int(math.isqrt(M)) + 1):
        if sieve[i]:
            sieve[i * i :: i] = False
    return sieve[1 : M + 1].astype(np.float64)


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Matrix builders
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
def build_toeplitz(seq: np.ndarray, N: int) -> np.ndarray:
    """Symmetric Toeplitz, T_{ij} = seq[|i-j|], i,j in [0,N).

    Requires len(seq) >= N.
    """
    idx = np.abs(np.arange(N)[:, None] - np.arange(N)[None, :])
    return seq[idx]


def build_hankel(seq: np.ndarray, N: int) -> np.ndarray:
    """Symmetric Hankel, H_{ij} = seq[i+j], i,j in [0,N).

    Requires len(seq) >= 2N - 1.
    """
    idx = np.arange(N)[:, None] + np.arange(N)[None, :]
    return seq[idx]


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Spectral-moment computation
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
def normalised_eigenvalues(
    seq: np.ndarray,
    N: int,
    kind: str,
    p_mean: float,
    p_var: float,
) -> np.ndarray:
    """Centre `seq` by p_mean, scale to unit-variance, build matrix, return
    eigenvalues divided by sqrt(N) (BDJ scaling)."""
    if p_var <= 0:
        raise ValueError(f"non-positive entry variance p_var={p_var}")
    s_centered = (seq - p_mean) / math.sqrt(p_var)
    if kind == "T":
        M = build_toeplitz(s_centered, N)
    elif kind == "H":
        M = build_hankel(s_centered, N)
    else:
        raise ValueError(kind)
    w = np.linalg.eigvalsh(M)
    return w / math.sqrt(N)


def spectral_moments(eigs: np.ndarray, ks: tuple[int, ...]) -> dict[int, float]:
    """Empirical even moments m_k = mean_{lambda} lambda^k."""
    out: dict[int, float] = {}
    for k in ks:
        out[k] = float(np.mean(eigs ** k))
    return out


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Nulls: (B1) i.i.d. Bernoulli(p) matched-density, (B2) random permutation
# of chi_P (matches multiset of values exactly), same matrix-type
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
def bernoulli_null_eigs(
    rng: np.random.Generator,
    N: int,
    kind: str,
    p: float,
    n_seq: int,
) -> np.ndarray:
    """B1: sample i.i.d. Bern(p) - p sequence of length n_seq, build
    Toeplitz/Hankel of size N (after standardising), return eigenvalues/sqrt(N)."""
    raw = rng.binomial(1, p, size=n_seq).astype(np.float64)
    p_var = p * (1.0 - p)
    return normalised_eigenvalues(raw, N, kind, p_mean=p, p_var=p_var)


def permutation_null_eigs(
    rng: np.random.Generator,
    chi_seq: np.ndarray,
    N: int,
    kind: str,
    p: float,

    Any deviation from chi_P here is from positional order (= prime arithmetic
    structure), not from value-distribution mismatch."""
    perm = rng.permutation(chi_seq)
    p_var = p * (1.0 - p)
    return normalised_eigenvalues(perm, N, kind, p_mean=p, p_var=p_var)

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
@dataclass
class NullStats:
    mean: dict[int, float]
    std: dict[int, float]
    z: dict[int, float]
    trials: int


@dataclass
class CellResult:
    N: int
    kind: str  # "T" or "H"
    p_N: float
    chi_moments: dict[int, float]
    bern: NullStats
    perm: NullStats
    chi_lambda_max: float
    chi_lambda_min: float
    chi_top5: list[float]
    chi_bot5: list[float]
    chi_bulk_moments: dict[int, float]  # excluding top-1 and bot-1

def _null_stats(
    null_arrays: dict[int, np.ndarray],
    chi_m: dict[int, float],
    moments: tuple[int, ...],
    n_trials: int,
) -> NullStats:
    mean = {k: float(null_arrays[k].mean()) for k in moments}
    std = {k: float(null_arrays[k].std(ddof=1)) for k in moments}
    z = {
        k: (chi_m[k] - mean[k]) / std[k] if std[k] > 0 else 0.0
        for k in moments

def run_cell(
    chi_seq_full: np.ndarray,
    N: int,
    kind: str,
    p_N: float,
    moments: tuple[int, ...],
    null_trials: int,
    rng: np.random.Generator,
) -> CellResult:
    t0 = time.time()

    chi_seq_used = chi_seq_full[:n_seq_needed]
    chi_eigs = normalised_eigenvalues(
        chi_seq_used, N, kind, p_mean=p_N, p_var=p_N * (1.0 - p_N)
    )
    chi_m = spectral_moments(chi_eigs, moments)

    # is the dominant outlier; for Hankel it's a +/- pair, so drop both ends).

    chi_bulk_m = spectral_moments(bulk, moments)

    bern_arrays = {k: np.empty(null_trials, dtype=np.float64) for k in moments}
    perm_arrays = {k: np.empty(null_trials, dtype=np.float64) for k in moments}
    for t in range(null_trials):
        e_b = bernoulli_null_eigs(rng, N, kind, p_N, n_seq_needed)
        m_b = spectral_moments(e_b, moments)
        e_p = permutation_null_eigs(rng, chi_seq_used, N, kind, p_N)
        m_p = spectral_moments(e_p, moments)

        N=N,
        kind=kind,
        p_N=p_N,
        chi_moments=chi_m,
        bern=bern,
        perm=perm,
        chi_lambda_max=float(chi_eigs.max()),
        chi_lambda_min=float(chi_eigs.min()),

        help="matrix sizes",
    )
    ap.add_argument("--moments", type=int, nargs="+", default=[2, 4, 6, 8])
    ap.add_argument("--null-trials", type=int, default=50)
    ap.add_argument("--seed", type=int, default=20260428)
    ap.add_argument("--out-json", type=str, default=None)
    args = ap.parse_args()

    Ns = sorted(set(args.Ns))
    rng = np.random.default_rng(args.seed)
    moments = tuple(args.moments)

    # Pre-sieve enough chi_P
    M_needed = 2 * max(Ns) + 5
    chi_full = sieve_chi_p(M_needed)
    print(f"[sieve] generated chi_P on [1, {M_needed}], "

        n_seq = 2 * N - 1
        p_N = float(chi_full[:n_seq].mean())
        for kind in ("T", "H"):
            print(f"[cell] N={N} kind={kind} p_N={p_N:.6f} ... ", flush=True)
            r = run_cell(
                chi_full, N, kind, p_N, moments, args.null_trials, rng
            )
            cells.append(r)
            zs_b = ", ".join(f"m{k}:zB={r.bern.z[k]:+.2f}" for k in moments)
            zs_p = ", ".join(f"m{k}:zP={r.perm.z[k]:+.2f}" for k in moments)
            print(f"   chi: {r.chi_moments}")
            print(f"   bern mean: {r.bern.mean}")
            print(f"   perm mean: {r.perm.mean}")
            print(f"   {zs_b}")
            print(f"   {zs_p}")
            print(f"   lambda range = [{r.chi_lambda_min:+.3f}, "
                  f"{r.chi_lambda_max:+.3f}]   ({r.seconds:.1f}s)")

    # Summarize: max|z| across cells per moment k, separately for bern/perm
    def _max_z(attr: str) -> tuple[dict[int, float], dict[int, str]]:
        mz = {k: 0.0 for k in moments}
        am: dict[int, str] = {}
        for r in cells:
            stats = getattr(r, attr)
            for k in moments:
                if abs(stats.z[k]) > mz[k]:
                    mz[k] = abs(stats.z[k])
                    am[k] = f"N={r.N} kind={r.kind}"
        return mz, am

    max_z_bern, arg_bern = _max_z("bern")
    max_z_perm, arg_perm = _max_z("perm")

    print()
    print("=" * 60)
    print("Summary: max |z| per moment across all cells")
    for k in moments:
        print(f"  m_{k}: bern max|z| = {max_z_bern[k]:7.2f} at "
              f"{arg_bern[k]:<22} | perm max|z| = "
              f"{max_z_perm[k]:7.2f} at {arg_perm[k]}")

    n_tests = len(cells) * len(moments)
    bonf = 3 + math.sqrt(2 * math.log(n_tests))
    print(f"  total cells x moments = {n_tests}; Bonferroni-3sigma is "
          f"~ {bonf:.2f}-sigma raw threshold")

    out = {
        "config": vars(args),
        "cells": [asdict(c) for c in cells],
        "summary": {
            "bern_max_z_per_moment": max_z_bern,
            "bern_arg_max_z_per_moment": arg_bern,
            "perm_max_z_per_moment": max_z_perm,
            "perm_arg_max_z_per_moment": arg_perm,
            "n_cells_x_moments": n_tests,
            "bonferroni_3sigma_threshold": bonf,
        },
    }

    out_json = args.out_json or os.path.join(
        os.path.dirname(__file__),
        "bdj_toeplitz_hankel_chi_p_results.json",
    )
    # Convert int-keyed dicts to str for JSON
    def _stringify(o: Any) -> Any:
        if isinstance(o, dict):
            return {str(k): _stringify(v) for k, v in o.items()}
        if isinstance(o, list):
            return [_stringify(v) for v in o]
        return o

    with open(out_json, "w") as f:
        json.dump(_stringify(out), f, indent=2, default=str)
    print(f"\nWrote {out_json}")
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    raise SystemExit(main())

    rng: np.random.Generator,
    chi_seq: np.ndarray,
    N: int,
    kind: str,
    p: float,
) -> np.ndarray:
    """B2: random permutation of chi_seq; matches MULTISET of values exactly.
    Any deviation from chi_P here is from positional order (= prime arithmetic
    structure), not from value-distribution mismatch."""
    perm = rng.permutation(chi_seq)
    p_var = p * (1.0 - p)
    return normalised_eigenvalues(perm, N, kind, p_mean=p, p_var=p_var)


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Sweep
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
@dataclass
class NullStats:
    mean: dict[int, float]
    std: dict[int, float]
    z: dict[int, float]
    trials: int


@dataclass
class CellResult:
    N: int
    kind: str  # "T" or "H"
    p_N: float
    chi_moments: dict[int, float]
    bern: NullStats
    perm: NullStats
    chi_lambda_max: float
    chi_lambda_min: float
    chi_top5: list[float]
    chi_bot5: list[float]
    chi_bulk_moments: dict[int, float]  # excluding top-1 and bot-1
    seconds: float


def _null_stats(
    null_arrays: dict[int, np.ndarray],
    chi_m: dict[int, float],
    moments: tuple[int, ...],
    n_trials: int,
) -> NullStats:
    mean = {k: float(null_arrays[k].mean()) for k in moments}
    std = {k: float(null_arrays[k].std(ddof=1)) for k in moments}
    z = {
        k: (chi_m[k] - mean[k]) / std[k] if std[k] > 0 else 0.0
        for k in moments
    }
    return NullStats(mean=mean, std=std, z=z, trials=n_trials)


def run_cell(
    chi_seq_full: np.ndarray,
    N: int,
    kind: str,
    p_N: float,
    moments: tuple[int, ...],
    null_trials: int,
    rng: np.random.Generator,
) -> CellResult:
    t0 = time.time()
    n_seq_needed = N if kind == "T" else 2 * N - 1
    chi_seq_used = chi_seq_full[:n_seq_needed]
    chi_eigs = normalised_eigenvalues(
        chi_seq_used, N, kind, p_mean=p_N, p_var=p_N * (1.0 - p_N)
    )
    chi_m = spectral_moments(chi_eigs, moments)
    # Bulk = drop the (single) top and bot eigenvalue (parity major-arc spike
    # is the dominant outlier; for Hankel it's a +/- pair, so drop both ends).
    bulk = chi_eigs[1:-1]
    chi_bulk_m = spectral_moments(bulk, moments)

    bern_arrays = {k: np.empty(null_trials, dtype=np.float64) for k in moments}
    perm_arrays = {k: np.empty(null_trials, dtype=np.float64) for k in moments}
    for t in range(null_trials):
        e_b = bernoulli_null_eigs(rng, N, kind, p_N, n_seq_needed)
        m_b = spectral_moments(e_b, moments)
        e_p = permutation_null_eigs(rng, chi_seq_used, N, kind, p_N)
        m_p = spectral_moments(e_p, moments)
        for k in moments:
            bern_arrays[k][t] = m_b[k]
            perm_arrays[k][t] = m_p[k]

    bern = _null_stats(bern_arrays, chi_m, moments, null_trials)
    perm = _null_stats(perm_arrays, chi_m, moments, null_trials)
    return CellResult(
        N=N,
        kind=kind,
        p_N=p_N,
        chi_moments=chi_m,
        bern=bern,
        perm=perm,
        chi_lambda_max=float(chi_eigs.max()),
        chi_lambda_min=float(chi_eigs.min()),
        chi_top5=[float(x) for x in chi_eigs[-5:]],
        chi_bot5=[float(x) for x in chi_eigs[:5]],
        chi_bulk_moments=chi_bulk_m,
        seconds=time.time() - t0,
    )


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Main
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
def main() -> int:
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument(
        "--Ns",
        type=int,
        nargs="+",
        default=[500, 1000, 2000, 3500],
        help="matrix sizes",
    )
    ap.add_argument("--moments", type=int, nargs="+", default=[2, 4, 6, 8])
    ap.add_argument("--null-trials", type=int, default=50)
    ap.add_argument("--seed", type=int, default=20260428)
    ap.add_argument("--out-json", type=str, default=None)
    args = ap.parse_args()

    Ns = sorted(set(args.Ns))
    rng = np.random.default_rng(args.seed)
    moments = tuple(args.moments)

    # Pre-sieve enough chi_P
    M_needed = 2 * max(Ns) + 5
    chi_full = sieve_chi_p(M_needed)
    print(f"[sieve] generated chi_P on [1, {M_needed}], "
          f"prime count = {int(chi_full.sum())}")

    cells: list[CellResult] = []
    for N in Ns:
        n_seq = 2 * N - 1
        p_N = float(chi_full[:n_seq].mean())
        for kind in ("T", "H"):
            print(f"[cell] N={N} kind={kind} p_N={p_N:.6f} ... ", flush=True)
            r = run_cell(
                chi_full, N, kind, p_N, moments, args.null_trials, rng
            )
            cells.append(r)
            zs_b = ", ".join(f"m{k}:zB={r.bern.z[k]:+.2f}" for k in moments)
            zs_p = ", ".join(f"m{k}:zP={r.perm.z[k]:+.2f}" for k in moments)
            print(f"   chi: {r.chi_moments}")
            print(f"   bern mean: {r.bern.mean}")
            print(f"   perm mean: {r.perm.mean}")
            print(f"   {zs_b}")
            print(f"   {zs_p}")
            print(f"   lambda range = [{r.chi_lambda_min:+.3f}, "
                  f"{r.chi_lambda_max:+.3f}]   ({r.seconds:.1f}s)")

    # Summarize: max|z| across cells per moment k, separately for bern/perm
    def _max_z(attr: str) -> tuple[dict[int, float], dict[int, str]]:
        mz = {k: 0.0 for k in moments}
        am: dict[int, str] = {}
        for r in cells:
            stats = getattr(r, attr)
            for k in moments:
                if abs(stats.z[k]) > mz[k]:
                    mz[k] = abs(stats.z[k])
                    am[k] = f"N={r.N} kind={r.kind}"
        return mz, am

    max_z_bern, arg_bern = _max_z("bern")
    max_z_perm, arg_perm = _max_z("perm")

    print()
    print("=" * 60)
    print("Summary: max |z| per moment across all cells")
    for k in moments:
        print(f"  m_{k}: bern max|z| = {max_z_bern[k]:7.2f} at "
              f"{arg_bern[k]:<22} | perm max|z| = "
              f"{max_z_perm[k]:7.2f} at {arg_perm[k]}")

    n_tests = len(cells) * len(moments)
    bonf = 3 + math.sqrt(2 * math.log(n_tests))
    print(f"  total cells x moments = {n_tests}; Bonferroni-3sigma is "
          f"~ {bonf:.2f}-sigma raw threshold")

    out = {
        "config": vars(args),
        "cells": [asdict(c) for c in cells],
        "summary": {
            "bern_max_z_per_moment": max_z_bern,
            "bern_arg_max_z_per_moment": arg_bern,
            "perm_max_z_per_moment": max_z_perm,
            "perm_arg_max_z_per_moment": arg_perm,
            "n_cells_x_moments": n_tests,
            "bonferroni_3sigma_threshold": bonf,
        },
    }

    out_json = args.out_json or os.path.join(
        os.path.dirname(__file__),
        "bdj_toeplitz_hankel_chi_p_results.json",
    )
    # Convert int-keyed dicts to str for JSON
    def _stringify(o: Any) -> Any:
        if isinstance(o, dict):
            return {str(k): _stringify(v) for k, v in o.items()}
        if isinstance(o, list):
            return [_stringify(v) for v in o]
        return o

    with open(out_json, "w") as f:
        json.dump(_stringify(out), f, indent=2, default=str)
    print(f"\nWrote {out_json}")
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    raise SystemExit(main())

# D3 — Free probability + matrix models: BDJ Toeplitz/Hankel LSD on chi_P

**Session:** S204 (cross-domain attack)
**ATTACK_VECTORS target:** §D.D3 — free probability + matrix models
**Cross-domain ingredient:** Bryc-Dembo-Jiang 2006 *Ann. Probab.* 34, 1
universal limiting spectral distribution (LSD) of real symmetric Toeplitz
and Hankel matrices with i.i.d. entries.
**Channelled mathematician:** Bryc / Voiculescu (operator-algebra free
probability rigour); Hammond-Miller 2005 (good-pair-partition expansion
of Toeplitz LSD moments).

## Pre-stated falsification criteria

For each cell `(N, kind)` with `kind ∈ {T (Toeplitz), H (Hankel)}` and
N ∈ {500, 1000, 2000, 3500}, we compute even spectral moments
`m_k := mean_{lambda} lambda^k` for `k ∈ {2, 4, 6, 8}` after centring the
chi_P entries (subtract `p_N`), standardising to unit variance (divide by
`sqrt(p_N(1-p_N))`), and dividing eigenvalues by `sqrt(N)` (the BDJ
normalisation).

Two nulls (matched first-2-moments):

- **B1 — i.i.d. Bernoulli(p_N).** Random Toeplitz/Hankel built from i.i.d.
  Bernoulli sequence with the same density. This is the BDJ universal-LSD
  baseline (since the limiting moments depend only on entry variance).
- **B2 — random permutation of chi_P[1..2N-1].** Same multiset of values
  as chi_P, in random order. Any chi_P deviation from B2 reflects
  **arithmetic positional order**, not value-distribution mismatch.

**Outcomes:**

- **(I, A-grade success):** chi_P moment `m_k` differs from BOTH null means
  by `>= 3 sigma` at some `k ≥ 4`, growing with N reproducibly,
  AND the deviation cannot be reduced to a known E2.21-class
  Hardy-Littlewood-spike effect. → genuine new free-probability fingerprint
  for chi_P.
- **(I, B-grade case (i)):** chi_P moments deviate from BDJ universal limit
  reproducibly, with the deviation EXPLAINED quantitatively by an
  identifiable major-arc spike (E2.21 mechanism). → first project
  measurement of the chi_P symbol's L^k norms via Toeplitz spectral
  moments; refines E2.21 from the L^∞ point-evaluation domain to the
  L^k integral-evaluation domain. New scaling formula testable.
- **(E, B-grade orthogonality):** chi_P moments match BDJ universal limit
  / both nulls within `+- 2 sigma`. → 15th orthogonal pseudorandomness
  category; chi_P-Toeplitz spectrum is BDJ-universal.
- **(INC):** noise dominates signal at tested scales; need N ≥ 10^4 with
  prohibitive eigensolve cost.

## Theoretical predictions (pre-experiment, derived from E2.21 + Szegő)

E2.21 establishes `|F_N(e^{2πi a/q})| ≈ μ²(q)/φ(q) · π(N)`, with the
dominant peak at `q = 2` (parity major arc) of magnitude `≈ π(N)`. For
the centered standardised chi_P-Toeplitz of size N, this translates to a
single isolated eigenvalue (the "parity outlier") of magnitude
`λ̃_max ≈ c · sqrt(N / log N)` for some constant `c` of order 1 — verified
in the smoke test as `c ≈ 1.26 ± 0.02` across N ∈ {500, 1000, 2000}.

**Scaling prediction:**

  `λ̃_max(chi_P-T, N) ≈ c · sqrt(N / log N), c ≈ 1.26`

  `m_4(chi_P-T, N) ≈ A · N / log² N + (BDJ baseline 8/3)`

  `m_6(chi_P-T, N) ≈ B · N² / log³ N + (BDJ baseline ≈ 11.67)`

with the leading terms growing polynomially in N — i.e. m_4, m_6 → ∞ as
N → ∞ for chi_P, in stark contrast to BDJ universality (which has
finite limits).

For Hankel: parity-spike contributes a `±` pair (Hankel symmetry under
antidiagonal exchange), so the same per-side analysis applies with `top-2`
instead of `top-1`.

**Verification protocol:** for each N, decompose
  `m_4(chi_P) = m_4(top-1 contribution) + m_4(bulk)`
where the top-1 contribution is `λ_max^k / N`. The prediction is:
top-1 contributes ≥ 80% of m_4 at all tested N (smoke test gave 89%).

## Closure mode (to be filled after run)

[ ] I (A-grade success: novel non-E2.21 free-probability fingerprint)
[ ] I (B-grade case (i): E2.21-spike-explained spectral-moment refinement)
[ ] E (B-grade orthogonality category 15)
[ ] INC (noise dominates)

## Distinction from prior project work

- **CLOSED line 690 (R-transform of prime indicator):** used trivial
  diagonal embedding `A_N = diag(1_P)`, idempotent, ESD =
  `(1-π(N)/N)δ_0 + (π(N)/N)δ_1`, encoded only π(N). The Toeplitz/Hankel
  embedding here is structurally distinct: T_{ij} = χ_P(|i-j|+1) MIXES
  the prime indicator at all offsets, producing a non-trivial continuous
  spectrum after centring/normalising.
- **S74 (Marchenko-Pastur on chi_P MPS-Gram):** different matrix model —
  MPS-unfolded Gram matrix at scale R, gives MP bulk + spike outliers
  with k* ~ R^{0.85}. Toeplitz/Hankel here uses raw χ_P sequence at
  scale N, not unfolded; gives a SINGLE parity outlier (q=2) plus bulk.
- **E2.21 (Newman L^∞ flatness):** evaluates `|f_N(e^{iθ})|` at single
  rational points θ = 2πa/q. Toeplitz/Hankel m_k are L^k-NORM integrals
  of the same symbol. So the present work is the L^k generalisation of
  E2.21 from L^∞ point-evaluation, accessed via Szegő-Toeplitz spectral
  moments (free-probability framework).

## Cross-domain references

- **Bryc, Dembo, Jiang 2006** *Ann. Probab.* 34, 1-38 = arXiv:math/0307330.
  "Spectral measure of large random Hankel, Markov and Toeplitz matrices."
  Establishes universal LSDs γ_T, γ_H for symmetric Toeplitz/Hankel with
  i.i.d. variance-1 entries; eigenvalues / sqrt(N).
- **Hammond, Miller 2005** *J. Theor. Probab.* 18, 537-566 =
  arXiv:math/0312215. "Distribution of eigenvalues for the ensemble of real
  symmetric Toeplitz matrices." First numerical and combinatorial moment
  expansion via "good" non-crossing pair partitions; m_4(γ_T) = 8/3 (vs
  Gaussian m_4 = 3); the deficit is the "non-Catalan partitions" diagnostic.
- **Massey-Sinsheimer 2007 (REU)** Toeplitz with palindromic structure.
- **Voiculescu 1991** *Invent. Math.* 104, 201 — free probability framework;
  free cumulants κ_k via Möbius inversion on non-crossing partitions.
- **E2.21 / S138** (Newman L^∞ flatness of chi_P generating polynomial)
  for the specific spike-mechanism interpretation.

## Files

- `bdj_toeplitz_hankel_chi_p.py` — Python implementation (Toeplitz/Hankel
  builders, BDJ-normalised eigensolve, two-null comparison, top/bulk
  decomposition).
- `bdj_toeplitz_hankel_chi_p_results.json` — raw measurement data (cells,
  per-cell moments, null statistics, top-5/bot-5 eigenvalues).
- `run_full.log` — full sweep stdout.

## Results (filled after run)

  embedding here is structurally distinct: T_{ij} = χ_P(|i-j|+1) MIXES
  the prime indicator at all offsets, producing a non-trivial continuous
  spectrum after centring/normalising.

  MPS-unfolded Gram matrix at scale R, gives MP bulk + spike outliers
  with k* ~ R^{0.85}. Toeplitz/Hankel here uses raw χ_P sequence at
  scale N, not unfolded; gives a SINGLE parity outlier (q=2) plus bulk.
- **E2.21 (Newman L^∞ flatness):** evaluates `|f_N(e^{iθ})|` at single
  rational points θ = 2πa/q. Toeplitz/Hankel m_k are L^k-NORM integrals
  of the same symbol. So the present work is the L^k generalisation of
  E2.21 from L^∞ point-evaluation, accessed via Szegő-Toeplitz spectral
  moments (free-probability framework).

# D3 — Free probability + matrix models: BDJ Toeplitz/Hankel LSD on chi_P

**Session:** S204 (cross-domain attack, wild_swing slot)
**ATTACK_VECTORS target:** §D.D3 — free probability + matrix models
**Cross-domain ingredient:** Bryc-Dembo-Jiang 2006 *Ann. Probab.* 34, 1
universal limiting spectral distribution (LSD) of real symmetric Toeplitz
and Hankel matrices with i.i.d. entries.
**Channelled mathematician:** Bryc / Voiculescu (operator-algebra free
probability rigour); Hammond-Miller 2005 (good-pair-partition expansion
of Toeplitz LSD moments).

**Self-grade:** **B-grade case (i)** — refinement of E2.21 (Newman L^∞
flatness of chi_P generating polynomial) from the L^∞ point-evaluation
domain to L^k integral-evaluation domain, accessed via Szegő-Toeplitz
spectral moments. New precise scaling laws for chi_P-Toeplitz and
chi_P-Hankel spectral moments and λ_max, with a clean structural
decomposition (top-eigenvalue carries ≈89% (T) / ≈76% (H) of m_4
universally across N).

## Pre-stated falsification criteria (recap, before run)

For each cell `(N, kind)` with `kind ∈ {T (Toeplitz), H (Hankel)}` and
N ∈ {500, 1000, 2000, 3500}, compute even spectral moments

entries (subtract `p_N`), standardising to unit variance (divide by
`sqrt(p_N(1-p_N))`), and dividing eigenvalues by `sqrt(N)` (the BDJ
normalisation).

Two nulls (matched first-2-moments):

- **B1 — i.i.d. Bernoulli(p_N).** Random Toeplitz/Hankel built from i.i.d.
  Bernoulli sequence with the same density. This is the BDJ universal-LSD
  baseline (since the limiting moments depend only on entry variance).
- **B2 — random permutation of chi_P[1..2N-1].** Same multiset of values
  as chi_P, in random order. Any chi_P deviation from B2 reflects

## Closure mode: **(I, B-grade case (i))**

chi_P moments deviate from BDJ universal limit reproducibly across all four
N values, in BOTH Toeplitz and Hankel matrix types, against BOTH null
baselines (Bernoulli and permutation), with explicit scaling laws derived
from the Hardy-Littlewood circle method (E2.21 parity major-arc
mechanism). Per-moment z-scores grow polynomially in N, far exceeding
both the 3σ and Bonferroni-3σ thresholds.

`m_k = mean λ̃^k`. "Bulk" excludes the single largest and single smallest
eigenvalue (Hankel has anti-diagonal-flip symmetry `J H J = −H` so the
two extreme eigenvalues come in `±` pair).
